newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - November 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - November 14.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Thursday.
- A top-level report has uncovered evidence of widespread breaches and abuses of pay guidelines for executives in semi-state companies.
- Telecom Eireann's rivals in the mobile phone market, ESAT Digifone, have agreed a major deal to fit their antennae on police radio masts throughout the country.
- Deputy Prime Minister Dick Spring locked his Labour party into the coalition government for up to one year after backing the government in a confidence vote last night.
- Justice Minister Nora Owen is braced for further challenges to her authority after the government survived a confidence vote over a legal blunder which freed 16 prisoners.
- Strong economic growth means a new government plan could include tax reductions totalling 800 million Irish pounds over the next three years.
- President Bill Clinton is ready to send U.S. troops to Zaire to help the relief operation but they will not be asked to disarm combatants.
